events.text:
I don't think this level can be won under the rules as written, so I can't give you a winning sequence.

**What I checked with the tools:** The crystal at (7,1) sits on land and does not sink, and the wizard cannot walk onto water.

**Why it looks impossible:**
- The west island (door (3,9)) and the east island (where the bard starts, and where door (20,9) sits) are separated by 8 to 9 water cells. Nobody can walk across.
- The only ways across are wizard swaps. A swap exchanges the wizard with a hero or crystal in line, so every swap that crosses the gap flips the wizard's side and the other participant's side. The wizard, bard and crystal together keep the same side-parity throughout. That parity fixes the final sides.
- Door (20,9) is cut off by water on every side. The only way onto it is walking from (18,9) over (19,9), which needs a crystal sunk at (19,9). Only the bard's charm can push the crystal in, from the east island, and the bard must be on the east island when it does.
- At that moment the crystal and the bard are both on the east side, so the parity forces the wizard to be on the east side too. The sunk crystal is then unmovable, nothing on the west side can be swapped with, and the wizard can never reach (3,9).
- Using the crystal as a stepping stone on the west side instead leaves nothing to bridge (19,9), so door (20,9) stays unreachable.

I've reasoned through this by hand rather than proving it exhaustively with the checker, so the conclusion rests on my reading of the rules. If the checker has a mechanic I haven't modelled, that would change the answer.
